soundness_flags.label: Open-ended Question 1 (oeq:guoxu-separatrix-frontier)
soundness_flags.one_line: The phrase “a bounded-noise analogue” does not specify a recursion or noise-law class, so no single sharp margin or uniform attraction statement is determined alongside the exact Gaussian-noise Guo--Xu recursion.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: Theorems 1–4 and the finite-attractor class assumptions
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: Finite tail selection, positive basin mass, and the common Cesaro attraction modulus are assumed class membership conditions rather than derived for the Guo--Xu recursion.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: Field-tier conditional inference frontier: the stable limit, realized-QV pivot, and deterministic-sandwich frontiers hold for laws in the stated common-envelope finite-attractor class; Guo--Xu membership remains an open separatrix problem.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Abstract; Section 3.1, especially lines 337–348 of the HTML rendering
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper is titled “Statistical Inference for Misspecified Contextual Bandits”; it proves IPW-Z normality under scaled inverse-propensity convergence and uses a clipped, no-intercept LinUCB numerical example to illustrate instability and non-normality.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Theorem 5.14, lines 463–475; Design A, lines 514–518; Appendix Theorem A.1, lines 724–733
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper is titled “Fixed-Horizon Self-Normalized Inference for Adaptive Experiments via Martingale AIPW/DML with Logged Propensities”; it proves a realized-QV studentized fixed-horizon pivot without deterministic variance stabilization and exhibits two post-burn-in variance regimes.

The paper is titled “Efficient Inference after Directionally Stable Adaptive Experiments”; it introduces target-specific directional stability, contrasts it with full-matrix stability, and verifies its condition for LinUCB.
The paper studies off-policy M-estimators under misspecification and stabilizes adaptively induced variance using estimated conditional variance quantities and filtration-restricted weights.

The article gives a lower bound on convergence to a prescribed point conditional on its domain of attraction, supporting the proposal’s local-lock-in positioning but not a claimed boundary-uniform shrinking-margin result.

The paper concerns martingale CLT rates through normalized predictable quadratic variation and bounded increments, consistent with its limited use as a martingale ingredient rather than a finite-attractor result.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Replace “a bounded-noise analogue” with a fully specified reward/noise family, clipping rule, state vector, and quantifier over initial states; state whether the desired rate is for that family, the exact Gaussian recursion, or both.

Prove the attraction modulus for one nontrivial clipped-LinUCB subclass, or give an explicit near-separatrix lower construction; this would turn the conditional field result into a dynamics-derived contribution.
Normalize the bibliography to the verified primary titles and add exact anchors: Guo--Xu Theorems 3.2–3.3 and Section 3.1; Saco Theorem 5.14 and Design A; Shen’s directional/full-matrix discussion.

recommended_next_step: Revise the separatrix OEQ into one determinate bounded-noise model, retain the accepted conditional field-tier scope for Theorems 1–4, and correct the verified bibliography titles and anchors before Stage 0.
